subject: Follow-up: Healthfolio pricing scenarios, per-feature economics & CAC payback
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@healthfolio.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-06-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: inference cost and feature-level economics (Healthfolio)

Thanks for the call today — quick recap and asks below. Appreciate the concise run-through; we want to make sure we scope the PoC with realistic cost guardrails.

Recap from our side:
- Priority features: (1) Clinical triage (short intake + risk flagging), (2) Visit summary generation, (3) Personalized next-step suggestions.
- Current volume baseline: ~40k DAU, ~600k MAU; target scale for pilot is ~200k MAU over 6 months if engagement proves out.
- Typical session calls (rough averages from call): triage ~160 tokens, summary ~420 tokens, suggestions ~220 tokens.
- We need scenarios for $/1M tokens at three bands: conservative (low), baseline (expected), and worst-case (high). We asked for explicit per-feature $/feature, monthly inference spend at MAU tiers, and CAC payback math (we need to keep payback <= 6 months ideally).

Asks (next steps):
1) Can you produce a short tabular scenario: per-feature token assumptions, cost per feature at $250/$500/$750 per 1M tokens, monthly inference spend at current (600k) and target (200k) MAU, and margin impact given a target feature price?
2) Any quick wins on batching/kv-cache we can expect in PoC that materially lower the per-token cost?
3) Share a working sheet we can iterate on with our finance and product.

I'll loop procurement if we need to formalize terms.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Product, Healthfolio
alex.moreno@healthfolio.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-06-01T18:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: inference cost and feature-level economics (Healthfolio)

Alex — thanks, great talking with you and team. Quick answers and attached working file (inference-unit-econ-sheet-v1.xlsx). High level first, details in the sheet.

Short answers:
- We'll build scenarios at $250 / $500 / $750 per 1M tokens. Cost per token = $/1M / 1,000,000.
- Conservative per-feature token assumptions (we used your numbers plus 10% buffer): triage 180, summary 460, suggestions 240.
- Example headline: at $500/1M tokens, cost per token = $0.0005. So triage cost = 180 * 0.0005 = $0.09 per invocation; summary = 460 * 0.0005 = $0.23; suggestions = 240 * 0.0005 = $0.12.
- Monthly inference spend = sum_over_features[(cost_per_invocation * avg_invocations_per_user_per_month * MAU)]. We'll show current (600k MAU) and pilot target (200k MAU) scenarios.
- Batching & KV cache: for summary generation there could be a ~10-20% effective token reduction via prefix caching and response trimming in pilot; triage is harder to cache but benefits from batching if you can tolerate 100–200ms queueing. We'll flag expected gains per feature in the sheet.

Preliminary next steps:
1) We uploaded the sheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1hF-healthfolio-econ — open the tab labeled 'Scenarios' and you'll see three pricing bands plus sensitivity toggles.
2) If you confirm acceptance of the token assumptions we can finalize the PoC budget numbers and draft a simple pilot SOW.
3) I'll put Marissa on standby for procurement redlines.

Attaching: inference-unit-econ-sheet-v1.xlsx, quick PoC summary PDF.

Regards,
Karthik

Subject: Re: Follow-up: inference cost and feature-level economics (Healthfolio)

Thanks Karthik — looked at the sheet briefly. A couple of clarifications before we lock assumptions: 

- Our MAU breakdown: of the 600k MAU, about 45% will touch triage monthly, 25% requests summary, 30% suggestions. For pilot target 200k MAU we expect slightly higher engagement on triage (52%).
- Our internal finance constraint: CAC payback needs to be <= 4–6 months; target blended gross margin for the product is 30%+ after inference costs (we price the bundle feature at $2.50 ARPU/month initially).
- Acquisition assumptions: current CAC for similar features ~ $48 per new paid user. We need to demonstrate a 4–6 month payback window under each pricingband.

Can you show the math that maps: $/1M -> cost per invocation -> contribution margin per user per month (assuming average #invocations per user per month) -> months to payback given CAC? Please include three scenarios ($250/$500/$750 per 1M). Also call out where batching/kv-cache assumptions materially change payback.

If this looks good we'll route to procurement and product for sign-off.

Appreciate it,
Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@healthfolio.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-06-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: inference cost and feature-level economics (Healthfolio)

Alex — below is a concise worked example; full sensitivity table is in the attached sheet. I'll summarize each step so your finance team can follow.

Assumptions we used for the worked example (you provided / we validated):
- MAU (current): 600,000
- Pilot target MAU: 200,000
- Engagement: triage hits 45% of MAU, summary 25%, suggestions 30% (we flag pilot triage 52% in alternate tab)
- Avg invocations per active user per month: triage 1.2, summary 0.6, suggestions 1.0
- Tokens per invocation (buffered): triage 180, summary 460, suggestions 240
- Pricing bands: $250, $500, $750 per 1M tokens. CAC = $48, target bundle ARPU = $2.50/month, target gross margin = 30%+

Step 1: convert $/1M to $/token
- At $250/1M -> $0.00025/token
- At $500/1M -> $0.00050/token
- At $750/1M -> $0.00075/token

Step 2: cost per invocation (example at $500 band)
- triage: 180 * 0.00050 = $0.090
- summary: 460 * 0.00050 = $0.230
- suggestions: 240 * 0.00050 = $0.120

Step 3: average monthly inference cost per active user (weighted by invocations)
- per-user cost = (triage invocations * triage cost) + (summary invocations * summary cost) + (suggestions invocations * suggestions cost)
- Using invocations above: per-user = (1.2 * 0.090) + (0.6 * 0.230) + (1.0 * 0.120) = 0.108 + 0.138 + 0.120 = $0.366 per active user per month (at $500/1M).

Step 4: contribution margin per user per month (assuming bundle ARPU $2.50)
- gross_rev = $2.50; inference_cost = $0.366; contribution = 2.50 - 0.366 = $2.134
- contribution margin = 2.134 / 2.50 = 85.4% (note: this is before other variable costs; we only subtract inference cost here to show sensitivity).

Step 5: CAC payback months = CAC / contribution
- CAC = $48; payback = 48 / 2.134 = 22.5 months (this obviously misses your 4–6mo requirement under current ARPU).

Step 6: sensitivity across pricing bands (per-user cost and payback) — headline numbers (using same invocations):
- $250/1M: per-user cost = $0.183; contribution = 2.317; payback = 48 / 2.317 = 20.7 months
- $500/1M: per-user cost = $0.366; contribution = 2.134; payback = 48 / 2.134 = 22.5 months
- $750/1M: per-user cost = $0.549; contribution = 1.951; payback = 48 / 1.951 = 24.6 months

Observation: Under current ARPU ($2.50) and CAC ($48) the economics are far from a 4–6 month payback. To reach a 6-month payback with CAC $48 you'd need contribution ~ $8/mo (48/6), which implies ARPU materially higher or a much lower CAC.

What moves the needle:
- Increase ARPU: bundle pricing or premium upsell paths (e.g., charge $6–10/mo for feature set) — this directly shortens payback.
- Reduce CAC: target lower-cost channels or free trials that convert at higher rates.
- Reduce per-invocation cost: optimize prompts, aggressive batching, KV caching on summaries, or use a quantized/cheaper model variant for low-risk requests. With optimistic tech levers we model a ~30% reduction in per-user inference cost (see 'Optimistic tech' tab). At $500/1M with -30% cost: per-user = 0.256 -> contribution = 2.244 -> payback = 21.4 months — still insufficient alone.

Quick recommendation for pilot SOW:
1) Align on ARPU target for PoC (we recommend modeling a $5/mo priced bundle to understand elasticity).
2) Pilot technical optimizations: evaluate caching for summary and a cheaper model path for suggestions (target 20–35% cost reduction).
3) Work with product to instrument conversion funnel to reduce CAC by 30% via onboarding flows and targeted campaigns.

Next steps (concrete):
- Karthik: finalize scenario tabs and push an updated sheet with a 'path to 6mo' tab that shows combinations of ARPU/CAC/cost reduction required. (ETA: 48 hours)
- Marissa: stand ready for procurement routing once Healthfolio confirms pilot budget band.
- Lauren: set up a follow-up call next week with Alex + finance for walk-through of the model.

I'll attach the working file and the brief PoC plan. If you want, we can run a short internal exercise that shows required ARPU given a prioritized list of features (we already have that tab).

Regards,
Karthik
